data.narrative:
Baykar is a private-stage defense and security company founded by Özdemir Bayraktar. The valuation exercise draws from a comp universe of 10 peers: 2 public companies (DRSHF, IDEAFORGE.NS) and 8 private firms including Anduril Industries, Helsing, Shield AI, Saronic, and Quantum-Systems. The broader Defense & Security sector contains 23 comparable companies, though narrower peer cohorts at identical stage or valuation tier are limited.

Peer-median methodology could not be applied due to insufficient datapoints. Across same-stage, adjacent-stage, and similar-valuation-tier filters, the dataset yielded fewer than the required three comparable observations needed for a robust median approach. A full-sector median would introduce excessive heterogeneity and reduce analytical precision given stage and business model dispersion within the 23-firm Defense & Security universe.

Without triangulated valuation support from applicable quantitative methods, a defensible range cannot be established from the data provided. The analysis exposes a core constraint: Baykar occupies a segment of the defense tech market where public trading comparables are scarce and private peer financials remain largely undisclosed. Forthcoming data on recent fundraising rounds, revenue multiples, or loss trajectories among the named private peers would be necessary to enable revenue or earnings-based valuation. Until such datapoints emerge, valuation remains indeterminate from this framework.
